candidates.tagline: Cape Town's 50-year highway-to-nowhere finally has a plan: build another bridge, then demolish this one
candidates.story: Cape Town's Foreshore Freeway Bridge — a concrete elevated highway started in the early 1970s and abandoned unfinished in 1977 when the city ran out of money — has dangled over the CBD for nearly 50 years as a famous 'bridge to nowhere'; on October 2, 2026, Mayor Hill-Lewis unveiled the city's 'solution': build new alternative links over the next decade-plus, then demolish the old bridge.
candidates.why_funny: After half a century of a concrete highway hanging in mid-air, the official fix is a multi-decade plan to build a different structure nearby, then tear down the dangling original.
candidates.alt: Concrete elevated freeway structure in central Cape Town ending abruptly in mid-air, photographed looking east, with CBD buildings visible in the background — the famous 'bridge to nowhere' abandoned since 1977

candidates.tagline: SEGA sold 'all future paid DLC' then charged $30 for future paid DLC. Future came fast.
candidates.story: SEGA's Digital Deluxe Edition of Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds (up to $100) was marketed as including 'all future paid downloadable content' — but in October 2026, SEGA announced a Year 2 Season Pass ($29.99) for new crossover packs, prompting fans to publicly label SEGA 'stupid liars' and demand Year 2 content for free.
candidates.why_funny: 'All future paid DLC' turned out to have a remarkably short future — exactly one year — and SEGA apparently forgot they made the promise until the internet reminded them.
candidates.alt: Sonic the Hedgehog and crossover characters racing on a futuristic track in Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds, the game whose Digital Deluxe Edition promised 'all future paid DLC' before SEGA charged extra for Year 2
